result:
I found one native-rule issue and no stale-state or atomicity defects. Nothing was edited or run.

      "file": "browser/src/source/field-bag-actions.ts",
      "line": 91,
      "concreteTrigger": "Use an Ether or Max Ether from the Bag on a non-Egg Pokémon. Choose a target where some move, or every move, is already at full PP (for example the 'Restore which move?' prompt with move(39) at full PP, as the test at field-bag-actions.test.ts:103 does). The row is built with `disabled:!move.canRestore`, so `choice()`'s click guard (`!button.disabled`, line 28) ignores that move. The user can only press Cancel, which returns `{status:'cancelled'}` (line 92).",
      "impact": "This breaks a native rule: a healthy no-effect target gets reported as a cancellation. In native code, `PartyMenu_HandleUseItemOnMon` sends single-PP items straight to `PartyMenu_SelectMoveForPpRestoreOrPpUp` (src/party_menu.c:2420-2423), which lists every non-empty move (party_menu_items.c:935-938). `PartyMenu_Subtask_SelectMove` then calls `UseItemOnMonInParty`. If that returns FALSE (`MonMoveCanRestorePP` is false, use_item_on_mon.c:87), it prints msg_0300_00102 ('It won't have any effect') and exits without `Bag_TakeItem` (party_menu_items.c:970-982). In the patch, the native no-effect path at line 98 can't be reached for single-move PP items. A Pokémon whose moves are all at full PP can never produce `{status:'no-effect'}`. That goes against the contract that a healthy native no-effect result is its own outcome. Nothing is consumed or mutated, so this is an outcome and rule mismatch, not data corruption.",

Update the test at field-bag-actions.test.ts:103 to pick the full-PP move and expect 'no-effect' with State unchanged, instead of asserting the row is disabled."
